title: Cross-survey blending: every training view becomes a per-pixel mixture of the three surveys' photographs of the same place, so the model learns the continuum between surveys instead of three fingerprints
hypothesis: Four results in this era, read together, say the held-out survey fails for a reason no experiment has yet addressed: the model has exactly three appearance samples per place and nothing in training says what lies BETWEEN them. (1) Experiment 5 showed the gap is survey, not viewpoint: with a whole-frame trunk the three TRAINING photographs reached 72-81% usable at the same 11-17 m off-lattice eval viewpoints (train_capture_diagnostics 0.335 / 0.258 / 0.238) while the held-out 2024 photograph of the same viewpoints stayed at 12.5% usable / 42.3% false fix (1.298). (2) Experiment 3 showed that forcing the three surveys' features to AGREE does not transfer: its logged final cross-survey cosine was 0.935 (train_berlin.log, consistency loss 0.065), i.e. the three training appearances of each place were mapped to nearly the same 160-d vector, and 2024 got WORSE (false fix 65.3% -> 71.8%, 1.583 -> 1.648). Agreement on three points constrains two directions of appearance space per place; a fourth survey lands somewhere else. (3) Experiment 4's photometric randomisation (kept, 1.583 -> 1.271) covers the GLOBAL part of a survey change - exposure, colour pipeline, sharpness - and cannot synthesise the CONTENT part: leaf-on vs leaf-off canopy, shadow direction and length, parked cars, construction, the leaning roofs of a standard DOP vs a true-ortho. (4) A model-free design-time probe on the three TRAINING captures only (runs/_probe_exp6_scale.py; the eval capture was never opened): over 600 random lattice places, nearest-neighbour retrieval by per-crop standardised pixel correlation identifies a place across surveys from the SAME pixel-aligned viewpoint 90-97% of the time at 1 m/px (mean same-place correlation 0.49-0.57), rising only to 0.60-0.65 at 8-16 m/px - so (a) pixel-aligned surveys share most of their structure and a representation that locates one from another is not asking the impossible, (b) the survey difference is broadband, not fine texture, so a coarse-scale bottleneck is NOT the lever (that candidate was considered and dropped on this measurement), and (c) the same probe collapses to 7-11% under a 12 px shift and 1% under shift+rotation, confirming that viewpoint tolerance is the CNN's learned contribution and must be learned jointly with survey tolerance, not bolted on at decode. What the training signal lacks is DENSITY along the survey axis. The captures are pixel-aligned on one grid (alignment <= 1 px) and extract_chunk already pulls each position from all three captures under one shared heading, so a convex per-pixel combination of the three crops is a physically meaningful synthetic photograph of the same place: half summer canopy and half leaf-off, a shadow at an intermediate strength, a car at half opacity. With a SPATIALLY VARYING weight field, one frame holds a leafy tree beside a bare one, east shadows beside west shadows - states no real survey contains - so canopy, shadow, movable objects and colour pipeline become locally uninformative, while road, block, building-footprint and water geometry, which every blend renders crisply because it is identical in all three sources, stays the only cue that always pays. This is mixup/CutMix applied along the survey axis of aligned imagery; it is possible only because of this era's data asset (every earlier era had one photograph, and no row in lineage_history mentions mixing or blending across photographs), and it is a materially different angle from experiment 3: instead of asking the features of three fixed points to agree, it asks the classifier to be correct on the whole simplex between them, which is where a fourth survey is far more likely to fall than on any one of the three vertices. Capacity spent on three pixel-exact fingerprints per cell is capacity the blend augmentation makes worthless; capacity spent on shared geometry is rewarded on every blend and - the bet - on truedop_2024.
method: ONE change, in model/train.py only: a cross-survey blend stage applied on the device to every mini-batch BEFORE augment_views(). For each view in the batch, gather the three sibling crops of its position (same cx, cy and heading, one per training capture; the chunk is position-major so they are x_u8[p*K + k]), draw a smooth random weight field over the three captures (a 4x4 grid of Gaussian logits scaled by a per-view temperature tau ~ U(0.5, 3.0), bilinearly upsampled to 128x128, softmax over the capture axis) and replace the view by the per-pixel convex combination of its three siblings; with probability 1 - P_MIX (P_MIX = 0.75) the view keeps its own single-survey crop unchanged. Labels (position, bilinear tent cell target, residual offset target) are unchanged because the place is unchanged. Views per epoch, batch size, paired-position chunking, photometric augmentation, loss, model, decode, schedule and ONNX export are untouched; the exported graph is byte-for-byte the same architecture (3,079,093 bytes).
expected_outcome: Primary (held-out truedop_2024): 1.271 -> predicted 1.00-1.15, through BOTH product rates: usable_fix_rate 11.75% -> 18-28% and false_fix_rate 38.75% -> 28-34%, with 2024 coverage staying in 0.45-0.60 (currently 0.505; the 0.2 floor is not at risk). Median 2024 error (1,911 m) should fall below 1,000 m as confident predictions stop collapsing onto look-alike cells of a different survey. train_capture_diagnostics (bb_dop20 / truedop_2022 / truedop_2023 = 0.733 / 0.673 / 0.518 on experiment 4) are predicted to stay roughly where they are or drift slightly worse (0.55-0.85 each): the trunk is already underfitting (loss still falling at epoch 8) and blends make the task harder on the training photographs by design - a NARROWING gap between the training-survey diagnostics and the 2024 score is the evidence, not a rise in the diagnostics. Mechanical checks that must hold or the mechanism did not bite: the logged blend fraction reads ~0.75; the per-epoch top1 on blended views ends within ~0.10 of top1 on unblended views (if blends stay far harder, the model is still keying on single-survey cues); loss at epoch 8 is above experiment 4's 4.08 (harder task), not below. Decision rules: (a) 2024 usable up AND false fix down -> supported: the survey continuum transfers; the next experiment puts experiment 5's whole-frame trunk back on top of it (its fit gain on the training surveys may now transfer) or adds +-12 px vantage jitter. (b) 2024 unchanged (>= 1.22) while the training diagnostics fall -> 2024 lies outside the hull the three surveys span, synthetic appearance is not enough; the next move is a cached permissively-licensed teacher (DINOv2 patch-feature distillation with a cross-survey term, library L2 rank 3) or the mapping/query confidence split (L2 rank 6) to convert false fixes into abstentions. (c) false fix falls but usable stays flat (score 1.15-1.25) -> the blends taught honesty, not accuracy: still a kept improvement, and the next step is capacity/trunk, not more augmentation. Standing check: the score must move through usable_fix_rate and false_fix_rate; model bytes must read 3,079,093 and latency stays far under 250 ms.
eli5: The model has seen Berlin in three different aerial photographs: one in summer, one in winter with bare trees, one in early spring. So far it could pass its training by learning each photograph by heart - three separate memories of every street - and a brand-new fourth photograph matched none of them. We now show it, while it learns, pictures that are blends of the three: half summer and half winter, or winter on the left side of the frame and spring on the right. In a blend, no single photograph's look can be trusted, but the shapes of the roads, blocks and canals are the same in all three and come through sharp every time. The hope is that the model is pushed to remember the city by its shape, and that a photograph it has never seen then looks like just another blend.

stages.name: Camera frame
stages.detail: 128×128 px daytime crop, Berlin only; trained on three survey photographs, scored on a fourth it never saw

stages.name: Feature extractor
stages.detail: small strided conv stack that turns the frame into a compact texture fingerprint (last layer 160 channels)

stages.name: Map-cell classifier
stages.detail: scores all ~3,000 128 m map tiles of Berlin and picks the tile this view belongs to — localization as multiple choice, not coordinate guessing

stages.name: Local belief pooling
stages.detail: gathers the belief spread over the winning tile AND its 8 neighbours, and places the fix at the balance point of that local cluster instead of snapping to one tile's centre

stages.name: Within-cell offset
stages.detail: small head that nudges the fix from the pooled balance point to the exact spot

stages.name: Confidence gate
stages.detail: confidence = the belief mass on the winning tile plus its 8 neighbours — a vote split across adjacent tiles still counts as knowing where you are; belief scattered across distant tiles still reads as unsure and the drone abstains

stages.name: Training signal
stages.detail: NEW: three out of four training views are a per-pixel BLEND of the same place as photographed by all three surveys — summer, leaf-off and early spring mixed with a smooth, randomly varying weight map, so one frame can hold a leafy tree beside a bare one — before the usual random re-photographing (brightness, contrast, blur, grain). Only the shared street-and-building geometry survives every blend. Tile labels, loss, paired three-survey batches, schedule and views per epoch unchanged.

implementation_brief:
Edit model/train.py ONLY. model/model.py is untouched (architecture, decode, loss and export stay byte-identical; the exported ONNX must still be 3,079,093 bytes).

1. CONSTANT. Next to AUG add:
   MIX = dict(p=0.75, grid=4, tau=(0.5, 3.0))
   # p: probability a training view is replaced by a cross-survey blend;
   # grid: edge of the low-res weight-logit grid (4 -> ~32 m blobs);
   # tau: per-view logit scale range (small = soft everywhere-blend, large = patchwork of surveys).

2. NEW FUNCTION cross_survey_blend(x_u8, idx, cap_idx, n_caps, device, mix=MIX) -> (xb, mixed_mask, mean_max_w).
   Contract: x_u8 is the chunk tensor returned by extract_chunk (uint8 [N*K,3,H,W], POSITION-MAJOR: view j belongs to position j // K and capture j % K - this ordering is produced by extract_chunk's `for i in indices: for k, img in enumerate(imgs)` loop and must be relied on, not re-derived); idx is the LongTensor of chunk indices for this mini-batch (from perm); cap_idx is the chunk's capture index tensor; n_caps = K.
   Steps, fully vectorised on `device`:
   a. B = len(idx); p_idx = idx // n_caps; sib = (p_idx.unsqueeze(1) * n_caps + torch.arange(n_caps)).reshape(-1)  # [B*K]
   b. S = x_u8[sib].to(device).float().div_(255.0).view(B, n_caps, 3, H, W)  # all three siblings of every view's position, same heading
   c. own = S[torch.arange(B), cap_idx[idx].to(device)]  # [B,3,H,W] the view's own single-survey crop (identical to the old x_u8[idx] path)
   d. g = mix['grid']; tau = U(mix['tau'][0], mix['tau'][1], B,1,1,1); z = torch.randn(B, n_caps, g, g, device=device) * tau; z = F.interpolate(z, size=(H, W), mode='bilinear', align_corners=False); W = torch.softmax(z, dim=1).unsqueeze(2)  # [B,K,1,H,W], sums to 1 over K at every pixel
   e. blended = (S * W).sum(dim=1)  # [B,3,H,W] in [0,1]
   f. mixed = torch.rand(B, device=device) < mix['p']; xb = torch.where(mixed.view(B,1,1,1), blended, own)
   g. mean_max_w = W.squeeze(2).max(dim=1).values.mean() over the mixed views only (0.0 if none) - a diagnostic of how one-hot the fields are.
   h. return xb, mixed, mean_max_w.
   If n_caps < 2 (an area without captures) return (own, all-False mask, 0.0) - blending degenerates to the old path.
   Memory: S is [64,3,3,128,128] float32 = ~38 MB on MPS; fine. Do NOT build blends at chunk level on the CPU (800 MB float).

3. TRAINING LOOP. In train_area's inner loop replace
      xb = augment_views(x_u8[idx].to(device).float() / 255.0)
   with
      xb, mixed, mmw = cross_survey_blend(x_u8, idx, cap_idx, n_caps, device)
      xb = augment_views(xb)
   Everything after (cb, pb, logits, soft targets, residual offset target, loss, optimizer step) is unchanged - the labels are the position's, and the position is unchanged by blending.

4. LOGGING (so the record shows whether the mechanism bit). Per epoch, in addition to the existing counters: n_mixed (sum of mixed), blend_fraction = n_mixed / seen, top1_blend = top1 over MIXED views vs the containing cell, top1_unmixed = top1 over UNMIXED views, mean_max_w averaged over batches that had mixed views. Keep final_top1 as the overall number for continuity. Change top1_by_capture to be computed over UNMIXED views only (a blended view has no single capture) and say so in a comment. Extend the epoch print line with blend_frac=, top1_blend=, top1_unmixed=, mean_max_w=.
   In the returned info dict add: 'cross_survey_blend': MIX, 'final_blend_fraction', 'final_top1_blend', 'final_top1_unmixed', 'final_blend_mean_max_weight', and change 'capture_sampling' to 'paired-position interleave, shared heading per position, cross-survey per-pixel blend (MIX) then per-view photometric+sharpness nuisance randomisation'. Update the module docstring with a short CROSS-SURVEY BLEND paragraph mirroring the NUISANCE RANDOMISATION one.

5. CONTRACTS TO PRESERVE (the frozen scorer depends on them):
   - train.py CLI unchanged: --area --out-dir --data-dir --epochs --max-crops-per-bucket --seed; writes <out>/models/<area>.onnx and appends to <out>/train_info.json.
   - Data contract: training reads ONLY buckets(meta, 'train') via load_scene; the eval capture (buckets(meta, 'eval'), truedop_2024) must never be opened by anything under model/ in any form. Blending uses only the training captures already in `imgs`.
   - ONNX export contract (model/model.py docstring): 1x3x128x128 float32 in [0,1] -> [[u, v, conf]], u, v normalised map coords, conf in [0,1]; export <= 4 MiB; host latency proxy <= 250 ms. Untouched here.
   - Views per epoch stay len(crops) * len(imgs) = 218,136; BATCH_SIZE 64, CHUNK_SIZE 4096, Adam 1e-3 + cosine to 1e-4, EPOCHS from the CLI - all unchanged. Wall-clock should match experiment 4 (~6,150 s for 8 epochs): the blend adds one gather and one weighted sum per batch on the device.
   - Python 3.11; no 3.12-only syntax. Syntax check: .venv/bin/python -c 'import model.train, model.model'.
